items.text: The death of 13-year-old Hannah Jacobs after drinking hot chocolate from Costa Coffee in London highlights the need for better allergy training. Hannah’s mother informed the staff of Hannah’s severe dairy allergy; however, a failure in communication led to a fatal reaction. This tragedy is similar to Natasha Ednan-Laperouse’s 2016 death after consuming a Pret a Manger baguette, which resulted in the creation of ‘Natasha’s Law’ in 2021. Campaigners argue that current allergy safety training in the food industry is inadequate and treated as a mere formality. They are calling for stricter regulations, including ‘Owen’s Law’, which would require allergens to be clearly listed on menus and more thorough allergy training for food service workers. Better awareness and education on the dangers of allergies, starting in schools, are also needed to prevent such incidents. Costa Coffee described Hannah’s death as a tragedy and emphasized the need for companies to improve their training practices. Difficult words: fatal (causing death), mere (not large or important). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Hannah Jacobs, a 13-year-old girl, died after drinking hot chocolate from Costa Coffee in London. Her mother told the staff about Hannah’s dairy allergy, but there was a mistake in communication, which caused a serious reaction that led to her death. This is similar to the 2016 death of Natasha Ednan-Laperouse after eating a Pret a Manger baguette, which led to the creation of ‘Natasha’s Law’. People are saying that food allergy training in restaurants is not good enough. They want stricter rules, like ‘Owen’s Law’, which would require menus to show all allergens clearly. They also want better training for staff and more education about allergies, starting in schools, to prevent these tragedies. Difficult words: dairy (a product which contains milk), creation (making something exist), allergen (a substance which causes an allergic reaction). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A tragedy happens at Costa Coffee in London. Hannah Jacobs is 13 years old. She drinks hot chocolate from Costa Coffee. Her mother tells the workers that Hannah has a dairy allergy. But the workers make a mistake. There is milk in Hannah’s chocolate. She has a bad reaction. She dies. This is like what happens to Natasha Ednan-Laperouse in 2016. She eats a baguette from Pret a Manger. She dies, too. Now, people are asking for better allergy training in restaurants. They want workers to learn more about allergies, and they want to see all allergens on menus. They also think it is important to teach children about allergies in schools. Difficult words: tragedy (a very sad event or situation), dairy (a product which has milk in it), allergen (a substance which causes an allergic reaction). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Alain Delon, a renowned French actor, passed away at 88. Delon became famous for his roles in classic films like Plein Soleil, Le Samouraï, and Rocco and His Brothers. He was a key figure in the resurgence of French cinema during the 1960s, often playing complex characters such as hitmen and romantic leads under the direction of some of the greatest filmmakers of that era. Delon’s striking appearance and intense performances made him an unforgettable star, and although he attempted to transition to Hollywood, he remained a prominent figure in French cinema. Delon’s career spanned several decades, and he also ventured into film production and directing. He was known for his reserved personality but left a lasting impact on the world of cinema. French President Emmanuel Macron and others have expressed deep admiration for Delon, calling him a French monument and an unforgettable artist. Difficult words: resurgence (a comeback), hitman (a person who is paid to kill someone), prominent (important or famous). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A famous French actor Alain Delon died at the age of 88. He had roles in popular movies like Plein Soleil and Le Samouraï. Delon became very popular in the 1960s and people recognized him for his good looks and strong acting. He played different roles such as police officers and hitmen in many films. Even though he tried to make it in Hollywood, Delon stayed more successful in French cinema. Delon also produced films and directed some later in his career. The French President, Emmanuel Macron, called Delon a French monument and praised his talent. Delon’s children announced his death. They said that he died peacefully at home. Difficult words: recognize (to know or remember), hitman (a person who gets money to kill someone), praise (to express that you like or respect something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A famous French actor Alain Delon dies. He is 88 years old. Delon plays in movies like Plein Soleil and Le Samouraï. Delon is very popular in the 1960s. People like his handsome face. He plays different characters like police officers and hitmen . His acting is very good. Delon wants to be in Hollywood movies, too. But he is more successful in France. He also makes his movies and directs some. People will always remember Delon as a great actor. French President Emmanuel Macron says that Delon is very special and important. Delon dies peacefully at home. Difficult words: handsome (good-looking), hitman (a person who gets money for killing someone), successful (when you are good at something and achieve what you want), direct (to control a film or play or the actors in it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Several EU countries, including France and Italy, are assisting Greece as it battles wildfires spreading towards Athens. Firefighters found a woman’s body in a burned factory in an Athens suburb, and many people have been injured as the fires rapidly spread. The situation is critical. Firefighters are no longer facing a single fire but multiple blazes across various areas. Entire neighborhoods north of Athens have been evacuated, and residents watched helplessly as flames destroyed their homes. Strong winds and dry conditions have made it difficult to control the fires, with some flames reaching over 25 meters high. The fire has already burned through about 10,000 hectares of land. EU countries are sending equipment and assistance, including helicopters and ground troops, to help Greek authorities. The Greek government has faced criticism for not being better prepared despite efforts to control vegetation and setting up firebreaks . Difficult words: vegetation (plants), firebreak (a trip of open space in a forest to stop fire). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

France, Italy, and other EU countries are helping Greece fight big wildfires near Athens. Firefighters found a woman’s body in a burned factory, and many people got hurt as the fires spread quickly. The situation is very serious, there are many fires in different places. People who live north of Athens had to leave their homes because of the danger. The fires already burned through 10,000 hectares of land. Strong winds and dry weather make it hard to stop the fires, and some flames are over 25 meters high. Greece is getting help from other EU countries, which are sending helicopters and other equipment. Some people are unhappy, they say the Greek government didn’t prepare for this situation. Difficult words: spread (to move and cover a large area), flame (the glowing part of a fire). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some EU countries, like France and Italy, are helping Greece with wildfires near Athens. The fire is very dangerous. It hurts many people. Firefighters find a woman’s body in a burned building. Many fires are burning in different places. People must leave their homes north of Athens. Strong winds make it hard to stop the fire. The flames are very high. A lot of land burns. Other countries are sending help, like helicopters, to fight the fire. Some people think the Greek government does not do enough to prepare for the fires. Difficult words: wildfire (a big fire which spreads quickly in nature), flame (the glowing part of a fire), prepare (to get ready for something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

India has completed the construction of the world’s highest single-arch railway bridge. It’ll connect the remote region of Kashmir with the rest of the country for the first time by rail. The bridge spans 1.3 km over the Chenab River and is 359 meters tall, making it even higher than the Eiffel Tower. This new rail link is crucial both in times of peace and conflict. It’ll allow the transport of military personnel and equipment to border areas and strengthen India’s border security. Additionally, the rail connection will have a significant economic impact on the region, particularly for fruit growers who often face road blockages and landslides. Transporting goods by train could open up new markets, especially in southern India, increasing farmers’ incomes. Moreover, improved connectivity might boost tourism in Kashmir, which is already experiencing a rise in visitors. However, the region’s ongoing conflicts may limit the full benefits of this engineering marvel . Difficult words: crucial (very important), boost (to help to increase or improve), marvel (a wonderful thing). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

India built the world’s highest single- arch railway bridge. It will connect Kashmir with the rest of India by train for the first time. The bridge is 1.3 km long and stands 359 meters high, which means that it is taller than the Eiffel Tower in Paris. This railway is important because it will help both during peace and conflict. The military can use it to transport soldiers and equipment to the border. The railway will also help the economy in Kashmir. Many farmers in Kashmir depend on selling fruits, but they often have problems because of bad roads and landslides. The new railway can help them sell their products in southern India and have more money. The bridge may also bring more tourists to Kashmir, but ongoing conflicts may stop some benefits. Difficult words: arch (a structure with a curved top), peace (a period in which there is no war or conflict), ongoing (continuing to exist). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

India builds a very high bridge for trains. It is the highest bridge in the world. This bridge will connect Kashmir to the rest of India by train for the first time. The bridge is 1.3 km long and 359 meters tall. It is even taller than the Eiffel Tower in Paris. This railway is important because it can help move soldiers and things. It will also help farmers in Kashmir who grow fruits. Sometimes, they cannot use bad roads. They cannot sell their fruits. The new train can take the fruits to other parts of India. More tourists may also visit Kashmir because of the train. But there are still problems in the area which can stop some good things. Difficult words: railway (rails along which trains run), soldier (a person who fights when there is a war), tourist (a person who travels for fun). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A 19-year-old suspect was arrested on Wednesday for planning a suicide attack at a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna, Austria. The teen, who had pledged allegiance to the Islamic State group, confessed that he intended to use explosives and knives to kill a large crowd. The three sold-out concerts at Ernst Happel Stadium expected to attract over 195,000 people, have been canceled. Austrian authorities discovered chemicals at the suspect’s home, which he had allegedly stolen from his previous workplace. The suspect, who has North Macedonian roots, was arrested along with two others. The Austrian Chancellor expressed relief that a potential tragedy was avoided, and the investigation is ongoing to understand the extent of the planned attack. All tickets for the concerts will be refunded for safety reasons. Difficult words: pledge (to promise or be committed to a cause), allegiance (loyalty or support to a group or cause), extent (the degree or level of something that happens). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Police arrested a 19-year-old man in Austria for planning a suicide attack at a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna. The man supported the Islamic State group and confessed that he wanted to kill many people. He planned to use bombs and knives. Because of this, organizers canceled all three concerts at the Ernst Happel Stadium. 195,000 fans bought tickets to these concerts. The man has North Macedonian roots . The police found chemicals in the man’s home, and they found out that he stole them from his old job. The Austrian government is relieved that the attack didn’t happen. All fans will get their money back. Difficult words: suicide attack (an attack when someone knows that he or she will die too, usually using a bomb), confessed (to admit doing something), roots (where a family comes from).

Police arrest a man who plans an attack at a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna, Austria. The man is 19 years old. His family comes from Macedonia. He supports the Islamic State. He wants to hurt many people. He plans to use bombs and knives . The police find dangerous chemicals in his home. The man steals the chemicals in his old job. Organizers sell 195,000 tickets to three Taylor Swift concerts in Vienna. They cancel all three concerts. Many fans are sad. They will get their money back. Difficult words: support (to like an idea or person and say it openly), knife (an instrument which we use for cutting), steal (to take something without returning or paying for it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A tragic plane crash occurred on August 9 near São Paulo, Brazil, killing all 61 people on board. The turboprop plane was en route from Cascavel to São Paulo’s international airport when it suddenly entered a flat spin and crashed in the town of Vinhedo. Video footage captured the aircraft spiraling uncontrollably before hitting the ground and causing a large explosion. Although the exact cause is unknown, experts speculate that ice buildup or engine failure could have contributed to the loss of control. The plane’s black box has been recovered, and investigations are ongoing, involving both Brazilian and international experts. Authorities initially reported 62 passengers but later confirmed that 57 passengers and four crew members were on board. This crash is the deadliest in Brazil since 2007. Difficult words: turboprop (a type of aircraft powered by a turbine engine), en route (on the way), initially (at first). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On August 9, a plane crashed near São Paulo, Brazil. 61 people died. The plane took off from Cascavel and was going to São Paulo’s airport. While flying, it started spinning and crashed in the town of Vinhedo. The crash caused a big explosion. Videos show the plane spinning before hitting the ground. The reason for the crash is not clear yet, but experts think ice or engine problems could be involved . Experts found the plane’s black box , which records flight data, and are investigating it now. At first, the operator said there were 62 people on board, but later confirmed 57 passengers and 4 crew members. Difficult words: spin (to turn around in circles), involved (to be related to), black box (a device which records information). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A plane crashes near São Paulo, Brazil. All 61 people on the plane die. The plane is flying from Cascavel to São Paulo. It starts turning in circles. Then it crashes in a town called Vinhedo. There is a big fire when the plane hits the ground. Experts do not know why the plane crashes yet. They have a black box, which tells them information about the plane. At first, the airline says that 62 people are on the plane. Later, they say that there are 57 passengers and 4 crew members. It is the worst crash in Brazil since 2007. Difficult words: airline (a company which operates planes and takes people and things from one place to another), passenger (a person who travels by plane, bus, train, and so on), crew (a group of people who work together, usually on a plane, ship, and so on). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Monday, a US judge ruled that Google acted illegally to eliminate its competition and maintain a monopoly on online search and advertising. This is a significant setback for Alphabet, Google’s parent company, and it may change how big tech companies do business. The US Department of Justice sued Google in 2020, claiming it controlled 90% of the online search market. Google pays companies like Apple and Samsung to be the default search engine on their devices, which blocks competitors from entering the market. Google’s strategy restricts market competition and innovation. Future penalties could include ending exclusive agreements like Google’s $20 billion contract with Apple. This aims to invite new players and foster innovation, especially with the rise of AI, and to ensure that current dominant players like Google, Apple, and Meta don’t control the next wave of AI innovation. Difficult words: monopoly (exclusive control of a commodity or service in a particular market), setback (a reversal or check in progress), dominant (having power and influence over others). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A US judge said Google acted illegally to remove its competition and keep control of online search and ads. This news is bad for Alphabet, Google’s parent company, and might change big tech companies. The US Department of Justice sued Google in 2020. They said that Google controlled 90% of the online search market. Google pays Apple and Samsung to be the main search engine on their devices. This stops other companies from competing. Google’s actions stop competition and innovation . Future actions might end Google’s big deals, like the $20 billion deal with Apple, and help new companies, especially with AI. Difficult words: competition (trying to be better than others), search engine (a program which searches web pages and other information), innovation (new ideas). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A US judge says that Google breaks the rules. Google wants to be the biggest company in online search and ads. But the company has a monopoly , and it is a problem. This news is not good for Alphabet, Google’s parent company . Google has too much control over online searches. Google pays Apple and Samsung to be the main search on their devices . Other companies have no chance to do the business. Google’s actions stop new ideas. In the future, Google may not make big deals, like the $20 billion deal with Apple. The idea is that Google, Apple, and Meta do not have control over the business. Difficult words: monopoly (when one company has big power), parent company (a company which controls other companies), device (a machine or tool which people use for a specific task or activity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The World Health Organization (WHO) urges governments to improve their vaccine campaigns as COVID-19 remains an issue globally. WHO officials reported an increase in COVID-19 cases worldwide, with Europe seeing over 20% of tests coming back positive. WHO’s COVID-19 technical boss, explained that their data from 84 countries shows a rising percentage of positive tests for SARS-CoV-2. The positivity rate varies by region but remains a concern overall. Additionally, at least 40 athletes at the Olympic Games have tested positive for COVID-19 or other respiratory illnesses. Many countries are experiencing virus surges regardless of the season. This suggests that the virus circulation might be higher than reported. Governments must continue to invest in understanding the virus’s circulation and impact. Over the past two years, vaccination rates have dropped, especially among health workers and people over 60, which urgently needs to be addressed. Difficult words: surge (a sudden and great increase), circulation (moving from one person to another or from one place to another). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The World Health Organization (WHO) is telling governments to work harder on vaccine programs because COVID-19 is still a big problem. WHO officials said that COVID-19 cases are going up worldwide. In Europe, more than 20% of tests are positive. Data from 84 countries shows a rise in positive tests. The number of positive tests is different in each region but is still worrying. Also, at least 40 athletes at the Olympic Games tested positive for COVID-19 or other respiratory illnesses. Many countries see more virus cases in all seasons, which means the virus is spreading more than we thought. Governments need to understand the virus better and more people need to get a vaccine. Difficult words: region (an area), respiratory (related to breathing), spread (to move from one place to another). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The World Health Organization (WHO) says that COVID-19 is still a big problem. They want governments to vaccinate more people. There are more COVID-19 cases. In Europe, more than 20% of tests are positive. Data from 84 countries shows more positive tests. This is a worry in many countries. At least 40 athletes at the Olympics have COVID-19 or other breathing problems. Many countries see more COVID-19 cases in all seasons. It shows that COVID-19 is still here with us. Officials need to understand the virus better. People need to get vaccinated. Not so many people get vaccinated these days. This is a big worry. Difficult words: vaccinate (to give someone a vaccine), data (information), virus (a small organism which makes you sick). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Friday, Russia disclosed the names of some Russians involved in a multi-nation prisoner swap. Vadim Krasikov, a hitman convicted of murder in Germany, and Artem and Anna Dultseva, along with their two children, were part of the exchange. The Dultseva family had been living undercover in Slovenia, pretending to be from Argentina for eight years. Even their children were unaware of their true identities and they spoke Spanish at home. Sixteen people were moved from Russia to the West, including seven Russians who were critics of President Putin. Among the freed prisoners were Vladimir Kara-Murza, Andrei Pivovarov, and Ilya Yashin from Germany, who were thankful for their release but didn’t want to leave Russia. Three US citizens were also returned home, which was a success for officials who had negotiated for over a year. Even though the swap happened, there is no sign of better relations between Russia and the West. Difficult words: disclose (reveal), multi-nation (including several nations), hitman (a person who is paid to kill someone). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Friday, Russia revealed the names of some Russians involved in a big prisoner swap . Vadim Krasikov, a hitman in Germany, and Artem and Anna Dultseva, with their two children, were part of the swap. The Dultseva family lived in Slovenia as secret agents. For eight years, they pretended to be from Argentina. Even their children didn’t know the truth because the family spoke Spanish at home. Sixteen people moved from Russia to the West, including seven Russians who were critics of President Putin. Some freed prisoners from Germany were thankful but didn’t want to leave Russia. Three Americans also returned home, which was a success after over a year of talks. Even though the swap happened, experts don’t believe it will bring better relations between Russia and the West. Difficult words: involved (being a part of), prisoner swap (when two or more countries exchange prisoners), hitman (a person who gets money to kill someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Friday, Russia exchanges prisoners with some countries. This is called a prisoner swap. Sixteen people move from Russia to the West. Seven Russians are critics of President Putin. Some prisoners from Germany are happy. But they do not want to leave Russia. Three Americans go back home after over a year of difficult talks. Some prisoners go back to Russia for example, Vadim Kasikov, a hitman in Germany. The Dultseva family lives in Slovenia as secret agents. For eight years, they keep saying that they are from Argentina. Even their small daughters do not know the truth. All family speak Spanish at home. Now, they are going back to Russia. Even though the swap happens, the situation between Russia and the West does not get better. Difficult words: exchange (to change something for something else), critic (a person who openly speaks against someone or something), hitman (a person who gets money to kill someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Anti-immigration protests erupted violently across the UK, leading to police officers being attacked and injured. The police tried to separate the demonstrators from counter-protesters who were chanting anti-racism slogans. Many arrests were made during the disorder. The Police Federation of England and Wales noted that clashes were widespread in major cities and towns and warned of further violence. The UK government promised that those involved in the riots would face severe consequences, including arrests, prosecutions , and imprisonment. The Home Secretary emphasized that criminal violence and disorder wouldn’t be tolerated. This violence is the biggest challenge for Keir Starmer’s government, which is considering emergency powers to prevent more chaos. The unrest followed false online claims about a recent killing, leading to far-right protests across the country. Social media platforms, especially those allowing far-right activists, were criticized for spreading disinformation . The police are focused on maintaining order and preventing further escalation. Difficult words: chant (to shout or sing), prosecution (legal proceedings against someone), disinformation (false information spread deliberately). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There were violent protests against immigrants across the UK. Police officers got hurt. They arrested many people. Police tried to keep protesters and anti-racism groups apart. Officials said the violence was in many cities and towns and warned it might continue. The government said police would arrest the rioters and they would go to prison. The Home Secretary said the police have full support to stop the violence. This is a big problem for the government. The trouble started after false stories online about a killing, which led to many protests. Many people said that social media spread false information and supported protests. Police are working to keep things calm and stop more violence. Difficult words: anti-racism group (people who fight against racism), violence (hurting people and damaging things), rioter (a person who takes part in violent protests).

There are protests against immigrants in the UK. The protests are violent. Protesters and police officers are hurt. Police try to keep protesters and anti-racism groups apart. The protests are in many cities and towns. Officials say that they may continue. The government says that protesters can go to prison. The government helps police stop the protests. This is a big problem for the government. The trouble starts after false stories online about a killing. Social media spreads these false stories. Police are working to keep things calm and stop more violence . Difficult words: immigrant (a person who comes to live in a foreign country), anti-racism group (people who fight against racism), violence (hurting people and breaking things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Angela Carini abandoned her Olympic boxing match against Imane Khelif within 46 seconds, stating she had to preserve her life. Khelif, from Algeria, has been allowed to compete in the women’s boxing in Paris despite failing gender eligibility tests last year. DNA tests showed she has XY chromosomes, identifying her as biologically male. However, the IOC permits her to compete as a female since her passport states she is female. Khelif is a UNICEF ambassador, and she began boxing in 2018. She competed in the 2021 Tokyo Olympics where she was eliminated in the quarter-finals. Many current and former female boxing champions have criticized this decision, arguing it is unfair and compromises the integrity of women’s sports. Despite the controversy , Khelif fought Hungary’s Anna Luca Hamori in the 66 kg quarter-finals on Saturday. A win guaranteed her an Olympic medal. The IOC spokesperson emphasized balancing inclusivity , fairness, and safety in sports. Difficult words: eligibility (meeting the necessary conditions), controversy (public disagreement or argument about something), inclusivity (policy of including all types of people). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Angela Carini from Italy left her Olympic boxing match against Algeria’s Imane Khelif after 46 seconds. She said she did it to protect herself. Imane Khelif can box at the Paris Olympics even though she didn’t pass gender tests last year. Tests showed she has XY chromosomes , meaning she is a biological male . The IOC says she can still compete because her passport says she is female. Khelif started boxing in 2018 and fought in the 2021 Tokyo Olympics, where she lost in the quarter-finals. Many female boxers think this is unfair because she has an advantage . On Saturday, Khelif fought against Anna Luca Hamori from Hungary in the 66 kg quarter-finals. She won, and surely, she will get an Olympic medal. The IOC spokesperson said they are trying to make sports fair and safe for everyone. Difficult words: chromosome (a small part in the body which has genetic information), biological male (a person who is born as a man), advantage (something that gives you a chance to be better than others). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Angela Carini is a boxer from Italy. She has an Olympic match with Imane Khelif from Algeria. Carini leaves the match after 46 seconds. It is dangerous for her to fight with Khelif. Imane Khelif can box at the Paris Olympics. But last year, she does not pass gender tests . Tests show she has XY chromosomes . Men have XY chromosomes. Women have XX chromosomes. This means that Khelif is born as a man. But she can still compete because her passport says she is a woman. Khelif starts boxing in 2018. She fights in the 2021 Tokyo Olympics. She gets to the quarter-finals. Many people think this is not fair. They believe that she is stronger than other women. Khelif wins another match against Anna Luca Hamori from Hungary in the 66 kg quarter-finals. It is sure that she will get an Olympic medal. Difficult words: gender test (a test which says if a person is a woman or man), chromosome (a small part in the body which has genetic information), compete (to try to be better than someone else). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Italy, lifeguards were once admired for their strong and tan looks, but now, they are becoming rare due to a shortage of recruits . Daniel Gergaia, a 20-year-old lifeguard, takes his job seriously. He trained for months in the Adriatic Sea to get his license . However, Italy is facing a 10% shortage of lifeguards this summer because the training hours increased from 30 to 100. Lifeguarding involves significant responsibility and risk, as rescuing a drowning person is challenging. Experienced lifeguard Alberto Biagini, who has worked on the beach for 29 years, notes that young lifeguards prefer working at swimming pools due to the pressures and legal responsibilities. He supports his younger colleagues and stresses that being a lifeguard is not just about enjoying the sun but involves a lot of responsibility. Last summer, lifeguards in Rimini saved 75 people from drowning. It is harder to find recruits because students now have exams during the summer. Despite these challenges, Danielle enjoys his job and recommends it. Difficult words: shortage (not enough of someone or something), recruit (a new member of an organization), license (formal permission to do something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Italy, lifeguards are becoming rare . Daniel Gergaia, a 20-year-old, loves his job as a lifeguard and trained for months in the Adriatic Sea. This year, there is a 10% shortage of lifeguards because training now takes 100 hours instead of 30. Lifeguarding is a serious job with a lot of risk. Rescuing someone from drowning is hard. Alberto Biagini started working on the beach 29 years ago. He says young lifeguards prefer working at swimming pools because it is easier. He helps his younger colleagues and says lifeguarding is more than just enjoying the sun. Last summer, lifeguards in Rimini saved 75 people from drowning. It is harder to find new lifeguards because students have exams in the summer. The job is hard, but Daniel likes it and says other young men should do it too. Difficult words: rare (not happening very often), shortage (not enough someone or something), drown (to die in water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Italy, there are not enough lifeguards. Daniel Gergaia is 20 years old. He likes his job as a lifeguard . He trains for months in the Adriatic Sea. This year, it is hard to find lifeguards because training takes 100 hours now. In the past, it is only 30. Lifeguarding is a serious job. It is not just about enjoying the sun. It is about saving lives. Alberto Biagini works as a lifeguard for 29 years. Young lifeguards prefer swimming pools because they are easier. Last summer, lifeguards in Rimini save 75 people from drowning . It is hard to find new lifeguards because students have exams in the summer. Danielle likes his job and says it is a good job. Difficult words: lifeguard (a person who saves people who have problems in water), serious (not funny), drown (to die in water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the British seaside town of Southport, a tragic stabbing incident occurred during a holiday dance class themed around Taylor Swift. Three girls, aged six, seven, and nine, have died, and five other children, along with two adults, are critically injured. The attack happened on Monday, and a 17-year-old boy has been arrested. Home Secretary Yvette Cooper visited the scene and laid flowers in memory of the victims. The community is in shock and struggling to comprehend this horrific event. Taylor Swift expressed her deep sadness on Instagram, stating she was completely shocked. The suspect, originally from Cardiff, moved to Southport in 2013, and his parents are from Rwanda. The incident is not being treated as terrorism. Police are investigating to understand the motive behind the attack. Meanwhile, the community grieves, and many people visit the scene to pay their respects. The police are not searching for any additional suspects. Difficult words: comprehend (to understand fully), motive (the reason for doing something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Southport, England, three girls died in a stabbing attack at a Taylor Swift -themed dance class. The girls were six, seven, and nine years old. Five other children and two adults are critically hurt. The attack happened on Monday, and the police arrested a 17-year-old boy. Officials visited the scene and laid flowers. The community is very sad and confused about this terrible event. Taylor Swift said she is shocked and very sad. The arrested boy is from Cardiff and moved to Southport in 2013. Traffic jams are causing chaos across Europe as holidaymakers set off for summer vacations. In Germany, Croatia, and Slovenia, heavy traffic has slowed travel significantly. Hundreds of thousands of people participated in Berlin’s annual Pride parade. In many countries, LGBTQ people still face persecution and have fewer rights. Initially, Vanya’s parents reacted with shock and sadness, but they gradually accepted him. Despite the cheerful atmosphere of Berlin Pride, it highlights the ongoing struggle for acceptance worldwide. Vanya’s father has become an activist, and at Pride, the NGO Quatia invited parents from countries like Georgia, Belarus, and Russia to advocate for LGBTQ rights. They hope to spread love and support when they return home. Difficult words: persecution (unfair treatment based on race, religion, or sexual orientation), come out (to openly declare one’s sexual identity), discrimination (unfair treatment). A hydrothermal explosion at Yellowstone National Park surprised visitors and caused them to run for safety as steam, rock, and dirt shot into the sky. The explosion was possibly due to minerals clogging an underground pipe. No injuries were reported, but the explosion damaged a boardwalk in the Biscuit Basin area. Videos of the event show water and debris raining down over the park. Hydrothermal explosions are somewhat common in Yellowstone. They occur when underground water turns to steam. Similar eruptions happened in the Biscuit Basin in 1959, 1991, and 2009. Predicting these events is difficult as they can happen instantaneously . The Park Service will investigate if the explosion altered the underground system by measuring the chemical makeup and temperature of nearby geysers and vents. Despite the explosion, no changes in the volcanic system have been detected, and the park remains at normal activity levels. Difficult words: clog (to block or become blocked with an accumulation of thick wet matter), somewhat (rather), instantaneously (immediately). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

It is hard to predict these events because they can happen suddenly. Park officials and scientists will check if the explosion changed the underground system. Difficult words: hydrothermal (related to hot water), predict (to say what you think will happen in the future), geyser (a hot spring in which water shoots into the air), volcanic (related to a volcano). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Portugal, cork harvesting is a skilled tradition passed down through generations. Every summer, workers like Carlos Feras peel the valuable bark from cork trees. It is a labor-intensive process that requires careful handling to avoid damaging the trees. The bark grows back slowly, allowing for harvesting only every nine years. Portugal is the largest producer globally, and cork farming is vital to the local economy. The material is in high demand for its environmental benefits. Antonio Jose Matos, who has been harvesting cork for 43 years, highlights the job’s challenges and rewards. Cork’s unique properties make it valuable for various uses, from wine stoppers to insulation and even aerospace applications. Researchers, like Miguel No at the University of Aveiro, are exploring cork as a sustainable alternative to synthetic materials. Despite the booming business, the industry faces a shortage of workers, with fewer people joining the profession. The long growth cycle of cork trees shows the patience required in this eco-friendly industry. Difficult words: labor-intensive (requiring a lot of work), vital (necessary), synthetic (not natural). On Friday, a major tech failure disrupted services worldwide and highlighted the vulnerability of interconnected technologies. Cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike apologized after an update to its antivirus software, which protects Microsoft Windows devices from attacks, caused a global outage. This outage led to thousands of flight cancellations and delays and affected banking, healthcare, and payment systems. Although the software bug has been fixed, experts warn that manually rebooting each affected computer will take significant time and effort. Microsoft estimated that 8.5 million computers globally were impacted by the glitch , making it the worst cyber event in history. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre and Germany’s IT security agency have warned that scammers might exploit the situation. Despite the fix, it will take time to resolve all issues and clear backlogs. It is important to be prepared for such disruptions in the future and have resilient systems. Difficult words: reboot (to restart a computer), glitch (a small fault or problem in a system or machine), scammer (a person who makes money by tricking people). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
